learningObjective: Explain the role of StableHLO as a compiler-portability boundary between ML frameworks (JAX, PyTorch export, TF) and compilers (XLA, IREE, others).
stem: How is StableHLO positioned in the OpenXLA / IREE ecosystem?

options.text: StableHLO is a runtime engine that executes MLIR modules directly on GPU without any additional lowering; it replaces XLA's Runtime and cannot be used with any other backend such as IREE.
StableHLO is the low-level LLVM IR that XLA compiles its HLO into during backend code generation; it exposes hardware-specific instructions and is not intended to be portable across accelerators.

StableHLO is a versioned, stable operator set (specified as an MLIR dialect) intended to serve as a portable IR between ML frameworks and compilers, providing forward/backward compatibility guarantees so that a producer and a consumer built at different times can still interoperate.
StableHLO is a version-agnostic Python DSL layered on top of PyTorch; it converts arbitrary Python control flow into JAX-style pure functions at import time and requires no compiler.

explanation: StableHLO is an MLIR dialect specifying a stable set of ML operators with explicit versioning and compatibility guarantees. Its purpose is to be the interchange layer between framework front-ends and downstream compilers (XLA, IREE, or others), so a model serialized in StableHLO by one version of a framework can be consumed by a compiler shipped at a different time.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: it is not a runtime; downstream compilers still lower to their own backends.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: StableHLO is a high-level ML operator dialect, not LLVM IR.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: matches the StableHLO project mission.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: it is an IR dialect, not a Python DSL.

assumptions: The ecosystem in question is OpenXLA / IREE / MLIR-based compilers.
nonImplications: Does not imply StableHLO covers every op needed by every model; some ops still require framework-specific extensions.
Does not imply StableHLO replaces HLO entirely; XLA still consumes it and may lower via HLO internally.
